parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Odufor, Etche LGA survey stations. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 20.32 | 0.13606 | 0.13606
2 | 851.16 | 1.1039 | 1.2399
3 | 2511.9 | 15.803 | 17.043
4 | 1345 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as AK-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Odufor, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Groundwater Site Note: Station Odufor, Etche LGA**

The vertical electrical sounding (VES) interpretation at station Odufor delineates a 4-layer geoelectric profile:
- **Layer 1:** Resistivity 20.32 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$, thickness 0.14 m (depth to base: 0.14 m)
- **Layer 2:** Resistivity 851.16 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$, thickness 1.10 m (depth to base: 1.24 m)
- **Layer 3:** Resistivity 2511.90 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$, thickness 15.80 m (depth to base: 17.04 m)
- **Layer 4:** Resistivity 1345.00 $\Omega\cdot\text{m}$ (infinite extent)

Evaluating consecutive resistivity triplets:
- Layers 1–2–3 exhibit $\rho_1 < \rho_2 < \rho_3$, representing an **A**-type sequence.
- Layers 2–3–4 exhibit $\rho_2 < \rho_3 > \rho_4$, representing a **K**-type sequence.

Combining these yields an **AK-type** sounding curve, confirming the accuracy of the survey classification on file.

{"curve_type_stated": "AK", "label_issue_flagged": false}
